title: Taxation (country overlay)
examples: How do I figure out what tax I will pay on my salary?
What is the difference between GST and VAT?
If I buy something, how do I know if tax is included?

explain.say: Today we will look at how taxes work on money.
Income tax rates change depending on how much you earn.
This is called a tax band system for income tax.

items: Lower Income: Taxed at Rate A
Higher Income: Taxed at Rate B

explain.say: For example, if the first twenty thousand pounds is taxed at ten percent.
Then any money earned above that amount is taxed at a different rate.

faq.a: A tax band is a specific range of income that is taxed at a fixed rate.
asks: What are the brackets for tax?
Do I pay one tax rate for everything I earn?

faq.q: Is GST the same as VAT?
faq.a: They are both types of sales tax, but they have different names and rules in different countries.
asks: What is the difference between GST and VAT?
Are sales taxes always the same amount?

faq.q: Do I have to calculate tax on my whole salary?
faq.a: No, you only pay the tax rate that applies to the specific portion of your income.
asks: Do I use one tax rate for all my money?
How do I calculate the tax on different parts of my income?

faq.q: Is sales tax added before or after the price?
faq.a: Sales tax is usually added to the base price of the goods you are buying.
asks: Is tax included in the listed price?
Do I add tax to the final cost?

faq.q: Does my tax rate change every year?
faq.a: Yes, tax rates and the income bands are reviewed and can change over time.
asks: Will the tax bands change next year?

facts: Income tax rates are often structured using progressive tax bands.
GST and VAT are both examples of consumption taxes.
These taxes are applied to goods and services purchased.
The tax rate applied depends on the total amount of income or purchase.

quiz.say: If the first ten hundred pounds is taxed at zero percent, and the next five hundred pounds is taxed at twenty percent, what is the tax on the five hundred pounds?
quiz.why: The tax is calculated by multiplying the amount by the rate, so five hundred times zero point two equals one hundred.

wrong.0: This mistake assumes that since the first band was zero, all subsequent bands must also be zero.
wrong.1: This mistake forgets to multiply the amount by the tax rate.
wrong.2: This mistake might add the amounts together instead of calculating the tax on the second band.

quiz.say: A book costs thirty pounds, and the sales tax is ten percent. What is the tax amount?
quiz.why: You find the tax by multiplying the base price by the tax rate, so thirty times zero point one equals three.

wrong.0: This mistake incorrectly adds the tax rate as a whole number instead of a decimal.
wrong.2: This mistake forgets to apply the tax rate to the original price.
wrong.3: This mistake might multiply the price by ten instead of by the decimal rate.

quiz.say: If your income is twenty-five thousand pounds, and the first twenty thousand pounds is taxed at ten percent, what is the tax on the remaining five thousand pounds?

options.show: the tax rate for the lower band
options.say: the tax rate for the lower band

options.show: the tax rate for the higher band
options.say: the tax rate for the higher band

options.show: ten percent of twenty-five thousand pounds
options.say: ten percent of twenty-five thousand pounds

quiz.why: You must only apply the higher tax rate to the amount that falls into that specific band.

wrong.0: This mistake incorrectly assumes that the tax rate does not change when you earn more.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly applies the lower tax rate to the entire income.
wrong.3: This mistake ignores the fact that the remaining income is taxed at a higher rate.
